differences.what: the steep gable over the east flank's front bay, with its finial, and the small turreted dormer beside it: the build stands a plain hip (K01 stands a shaped gable on the street front only; liberty L-k01-217-e20th-3781)

the oriel: in the photograph it turns the north-east corner and rises to the wall head, where a copper cornice and a pierced copper cresting cap it; the build's oriel stands 0.3 m in from the corner and stops a metre under the eave under a shallow cone

the east flank's window column: the photograph's lights are about 1.2 m wide (the build's 0.71 m), the second storey's sill about 0.9 m lower and the third storey's head about 0.85 m higher than built (camera residuals -27 to -31 px and +19 to +27 px); the column's centre agrees (u 12.09 against 11.91)
the east flank's ground-storey light: round-headed in a moulded brick arch in the photograph, a square-headed sash in the build
the street front's two round-headed ground lights under the oriel, and the oriel's two tiers of three bent lights: where the photograph puts them
the flank's brick banding and stone courses: the photograph shows raised brick bands at the sill lines; the build lays one stone band

the date: a 2009 photograph of the surviving house, 105 years after the scene, is evidence of 2009 (AGENTS.md rule 11); the copper's green patina, the window grilles, the fence and the planting are 2009's and are not copied into 1904
